North ( 1991 p. 97) de nes institutions as humanly devised constraints that structure political, economic and socialinteraction. Such interaction between actors is based on formal rules (laws, property rights, policies, and so forth) and informal rules (customs, norms, and so forth) (Ostrom2006 ; Grundmann and Ehlers 2016 ; Spijkerboer et al. 2019 ). In this study, we aim to understand these rules as this allows us to nd out what prevents actors from different sectors from ful Iling integrative potential. The IAD framework by Ostrom ( 2011 ) is a renowned instrument for conducting systematic institutional analysis.It was initially developed in the 1980s as an attempt to structure the elements, categories of factors, and logical interconnections that explain how institutions work(McGinnis 2011a ). nodes.paragraph: We will elaborate on these scientific traditions and clarify what they can offer socioecological analyses in sustain- ability science, emphasizing the prospective contributions toward sustainability transitions and transformations. A critical sustainability science research program, as we describe it here, can help: (1) analytically bridge the sci- ences, (2) provide crucial critical insights into social pro- cesses and conditions that drive ongoing and concerning environmental changes, and (3) specify socioecological conditions for sustainability transitions/transformations and reveal structural process that can advance or impede them. We start by describing what we mean by critical research, as there are many ways to interpret this descrip- tor, and it has been applied in numerous ways. Next, we elaborate on the two foundational traditions for this critical research program, based in a specific philosophy of sci- ence and theoretical framework. We then take this theo- retical and methodological discussion and move it in the direction of application, using the example of research on sustainability transitions in agri-food systems to briefly illustrate what is gained through the approach, and what is prone to get lost without it.
